summary: Inference-time LLM optimization can cut API spend by 50-80% without sacrificing output quality, primarily by reducing token consumption and reusing computed work. The highest-impact levers—prompt optimization, prompt/KV caching, semantic caching, and model cascading—are mostly easy-to-medium to implement and compound together. Teams routinely reduce monthly bills (e.g., $10K to $2K) while also improving latency, since fewer tokens and cache hits mean faster responses.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (KV / prefix caching)
techniques.description: Reuse the precomputed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples, long documents) so the model skips reprocessing them. Providers apply a steep discount to cached input tokens.
techniques.savings: Up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Place your large static system prompt and few-shot block at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI cache the prefix, charging only ~10% for those tokens on subsequent calls.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by the embedding/meaning of a query rather than exact string match, returning a stored answer when a semantically similar request arrives. Avoids calling the LLM entirely on cache hits.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache with an embedding model so 'What's your refund policy?' and 'How do I get a refund?' resolve to the same cached response, skipping the LLM call.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, escalating to a larger model only when a small model's confidence or validation fails. Reserves expensive frontier models for genuinely hard queries.
techniques.example: Try GPT-4o-mini first and only fall back to GPT-4o when the mini response fails a validation check or confidence threshold, so most traffic stays on the cheap tier.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim redundant instructions, boilerplate, and verbose context; compress long prompts with tools like LLMLingua while preserving meaning. Fewer input tokens directly lower cost and latency.
techniques.example: Replace a 500-token verbose instruction block with a concise 150-token version and use LLMLingua to compress retrieved documents before injection.

techniques.name: Output Token Control (max_tokens + concise prompting)
techniques.description: Cap response length with max_tokens and instruct the model to answer concisely or in structured formats. Output tokens are often 2-4x more expensive than input tokens, so controlling them yields outsized savings.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=200 and add 'Respond in under 3 sentences as JSON' to prevent the model from generating long, costly, unnecessary prose.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) instead of large context
techniques.description: Retrieve only the most relevant chunks for a query rather than stuffing entire documents into the context window, drastically reducing input tokens per request.
techniques.example: Instead of pasting a 50-page manual into every prompt, embed it in a vector DB and inject only the top-3 relevant paragraphs per user question.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent requests into a single batched API call or use provider batch endpoints (often 50% cheaper) for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% reduction via batch API tiers
techniques.example: Send overnight classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get 50% off per-token pricing with 24-hour turnaround.

techniques.name: Structured Outputs / Function Calling
techniques.description: Force concise structured responses (JSON schema, enums) so the model emits only required fields, eliminating explanatory filler and reducing parsing retries.
techniques.example: Use OpenAI structured outputs with a strict JSON schema so the model returns {"category":"billing"} instead of a paragraph explaining the classification.

techniques.name: Streaming + Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream tokens and stop generation as soon as the required answer or stop sequence is produced, avoiding paying for trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence like '</answer>' so generation halts immediately after the answer block instead of rambling to max_tokens.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer for LLMs that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity to cut repeated API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, Apache 2.0); you pay only for your own infra/embedding costs

tools.name: Redis / Redis LangCache (semantic cache)
tools.description: Vector-based semantic caching built on Redis to store LLM responses and serve similar queries instantly, reducing token spend and latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source Redis; Redis Cloud paid tiers and managed LangCache priced by usage

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, fallback routing, model cascading, and spend tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source core free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo (custom)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform offering caching, cost tracking, rate limiting, and prompt analytics via a drop-in proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo (Pro) up to enterprise

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), RAG, and routing abstractions.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source framework free; LangSmith observability free tier plus paid plans from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that shortens prompts and context while retaining key information to reduce input tokens.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, model routing/fallbacks, load balancing, and observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$49/mo and enterprise pricing

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API routing across many models and providers, enabling price-based routing and automatic fallbacks to cheaper models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use the router; pay per-token at provider rates plus a small margin

quick_wins: Enable prompt/KV caching by putting all static system prompts and few-shot examples at the start of every request for up to 90% off cached input tokens.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your LLM to serve repeated/similar queries without an API call, targeting 60%+ hit rates.
Set max_tokens limits and instruct concise/structured outputs, since output tokens are the most expensive per token.
Route traffic to a cheap model (e.g., GPT-4o-mini) first and escalate to a frontier model only on failure or low confidence.
Trim verbose prompts and switch from full-context stuffing to RAG so you only send the few relevant chunks per request.
